title: Legacy SDK request normalizer for OpenAI Chat Completions clients
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Several customers integrate Redwood behind legacy OpenAI ChatCompletion-compatible SDKs that assume older request shapes and streaming event framing. When we started enforcing the canonical Redwood API shapes and structured output hooks, these clients began seeing broken streaming events, unexpected function/tool-call shapes, and validation errors for structured JSON outputs. Goal: Implement a lightweight request/response normalizer at the Redwood ingress (compatibility layer) that accepts legacy OpenAI Chat Completions request variants, maps them to our canonical internal request model, preserves streaming semantics (delta events), and maps responses back to the client-expected format with minimal latency and full telemetry. This ticket implements the request normalizer component, its mapping rules, tests, and a gradual rollout plan.
decision_log: 2026-03-06: Chosen approach -> ingress-side stateless transformer (no per-client persistent store) to minimize operational blast radius.
2026-03-07: Streaming will use our existing chunk framing, but we will synthesize legacy 'delta' event envelope for clients that expect OpenAI SSE framing.
2026-03-08: Function/tool calling mapping will convert 'function_call' string vs object semantics to a unified internal representation; responses will be re-serialized to match client expectation.
2026-03-09: We will not change model selection logic; the normalizer only rewrites shape and tracks a compatibility header for telemetry and rollback.
2026-03-10: Security review flagged potential prompt-injection header passthrough; decided to strip user-provided system-level headers and re-insert sanitized equivalents.
technical_notes: Input variants supported: messages array (role/content), content string + top-level prompt, name fields on assistant/user, temperature/stop/token limits in both snake_case and camelCase.

Streaming: accept legacy SSE event chunks that include 'data: {"choices":[{"delta":{...}}]}' and normalize into our internal delta stream; outgoing streaming to legacy clients will synthesize SSE frames with equivalent fields and original 'id' if present.

Tool/function calling: Detect legacy clients that send 'function_call': 'none' | 'auto' | 'name' and convert to internal 'tool_call' enum; when a tool call is emitted by model, produce both modern 'tool_call' envelope and legacy 'function_call' fields depending on Accept header.

Structured outputs: Support legacy clients that expect text-only JSON blobs. If client declared a 'response_schema' (legacy name) or our new 'output_schema', validate using the same JSON Schema; if schema mismatch, include 'choices[0].finish_reason': 'invalid_schema' and attach a human-readable error in the delta stream.
Latency: Transformation must add <2ms median overhead on ingress path; implement transformations in C++ runtime filter and fallback in Go for experiment branches.
Telemetry: Attach compatibility.header 'x-rd-compat-version' to upstream requests and emit metrics compat_request_count, compat_error_count, compat_latency_ms per variant.
Fallback: If normalization fails (malformed input) return 400 with an OpenAI-compatible error payload so SDKs can surface consistent errors.
Rate limiting: Respect existing token/quota enforcement post-normalization; do not duplicate rate checks before mapping.

Edge cases: Handle mixed-mode streaming where client starts with non-streaming, upgrades to streaming mid-request (some SDKs do this on connection reuse). We will reject mid-request protocol switches with a clear error to reduce complexity.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress accepts at least 6 documented legacy request variants and successfully forwards to internal runtime with identical semantics.
Streaming: legacy SSE clients receive well-formed SSE frames with delta events and identical ordering to native requests for 99.9% of test runs.
Tool calls: When a model emits a tool call, legacy clients that expect 'function_call' receive a payload matching their expected shape (name, arguments string/object depending on variant).
Structured output: Requests that supply a schema are validated; mismatches are surfaced using OpenAI-compatible error fields and do not crash the runtime.
Performance: Median added latency on normalized path < 2ms for HTTP REST and <5ms for streaming handshake.
Telemetry: compat_request_count, compat_error_count, and compat_latency_ms emitted and visible in the Console dashboard with filters for 'legacy_variant'.
Automation: Unit tests covering mapping rules and integration tests exercising live streaming and toolcall flows are included in the PR.
Documentation: Console-Docs page and SDK migration note drafted and linked in the PR description.
work_items: Implement ingress normalizer middleware (C++ filter) with a feature flag 'compat_request_normalizer'.
Add mapping layer for request shapes (messages vs prompt vs content) and header-based variant detection.
Implement streaming envelope synthesizer for SSE and chunked responses.
Build function/tool-call serializer that can output both legacy 'function_call' and new 'tool_call' shapes.
Create JSON Schema compatibility validator and error-mapping utility.
Add telemetry hooks and Console dashboard widgets for compat metrics.
Write unit/integration tests and create a chaos test simulating malformed legacy payloads.
Write docs + migration note and coordinate rollout announcement with Solutions and Support.
PR review and gated rollout to 10% of legacy-labeled traffic, then 50%, then global after 72h and no regressions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for each mapping rule (messages->prompt, content->messages) and header detection.
Integration test: end-to-end flow with legacy SSE client emulator, assert event order and reconstitution of delta fields.
Tool call test: mock runtime emits tool_call; assert legacy client receives expected function_call fields and can accept both string-encoded and object-encoded arguments.
Performance test: run 100k normalized requests through staging and measure added p50/p95 latency.
Chaos test: send malformed messages, unsupported encodings, and mid-request protocol switches to validate graceful failures.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Deploy code to staging and run the full test suite.
Step 2: Enable flag for internal traffic and run validation harness for 48h.
Step 3: Enable for 10% of traffic labeled 'legacy-sdk' with close monitoring of compat_error_count and overall request success rate.
Step 4: 50% rollout after 24h with no regressions; full rollout after 72h.
Rollback: toggle flag off to revert normalization; update PR with root-cause and permanent fix before re-enabling.
